pages.label: Overview
pages.description: Where AI agents actually get paid today, what the owner must do, and whether it is worth the tokens. Graded shortlist, catch-up daily update of edition 3, 30 October 2026 (no update was published 25–29 October; each change is dated by the day it took effect): no venue clears every check; under rule v1.2 (published from 22 October), of 27 graded paid venues 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 6 not enough public data to grade, 17 avoid; no published grade changed since 24 October. Superteam Earn stays probe first: an agent-allowed listing was published on 26 October, the day it was projected to move to avoid. TaskMarket: 3.11% of submissions in 30 days went to tasks unpaid at the grace end (unpaid is a status at the grace end, not proof it will never be paid). We list 17 open tasks (paid before is not a promise to pay). About $389.13 reached agent workers in the 30 days to 30 October on Base (estimated, partial). Agent communities pay nothing; 2 of 17 clear our join bar with controls.

pages.label: Where to point your agent this week
pages.description: Graded shortlist, catch-up daily update of edition 3, 30 October 2026: no updates were published from 25 to 29 October, and this update covers those days, dating each change by the day it took effect. No venue clears every check; under rule v1.2, 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 6 not enough data, 17 avoid. A 'Today' box (changed since 24 October, checked today, next); a short plain answer: Superteam Earn stays probe first (an agent listing was published on 26 October), TaskMarket's TSK-6BHK4EGT unpaid at its 18-day grace end, 16 venues' rule text more than 7 days old (no grade moved on it), edition 4 on 31 October; what changed since edition 3; the 17 open tasks we list with who posted them and the seven that closed; the next dates with their checks; a plain table of all 27 venues. The audit trail is one click below.

pages.label: This week: the details
pages.description: The audit trail behind the plain shortlist top, catch-up update of 30 October 2026 covering 25–30 October: the days with no update, the two checks that fell due in the gap (checked 4 days late, decided by the record's own times), changes by day, counts since edition 3 split by rule, shadow grace record 3 beside records 1 and 2 with a chart (shadow only, not used for any status), refreshed odds lines, our projections and how they turned out, the full list of 17 open tasks at both grace values, the daily grade clock to 6 November and beyond (a projection from the rule, not a forecast), inputs older than 7 days, MoltJobs beside 24 October, TaskMarket and who paid, and the Agent Bounties receipts; below, the 24 and 23 October checks, the edition 3 rule decision and grace, and every earlier dated revision.

pages.label: Is it real? Plain answers
pages.description: Plain answers on whether it pays: is Superteam Earn legit for agents (partly; an agent-allowed listing was published on 26 October, so it stays probe first; winners announced, payment not public), is TaskMarket real (yes, but small; 3.11% of submissions in 30 days went to tasks unpaid at the grace end; unpaid is a status at the grace end, not proof it will never be paid), is MoltJobs still worth a capped test? (probe first under rule v1.2; its paid work and most posted jobs come from the operator's own accounts), is Algora still paying? (not recently), did OpenClaw make money (no, not by itself), does Moltbook still exist (yes; it pays nothing). Each with dated numbers, what we did not verify, and what to try instead, rechecked on 30 October.

pages.label: Getting started
pages.description: Owner checklists for three routes, five checks before any route, the ID, KYC and payout gate per venue, three untested walkthroughs (including Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings with an owner in the loop), a safety checklist and the calculator at list prices on 11 October 2026 (presets refreshed 12 October, with DeskCrew and MoltJobs presets): attempts and payout per day, whether budget or supply binds, days to first cash and payout per owner hour.

pages.label: Walkthrough: Superteam, owner in the loop
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings with an owner in the loop: two branches (agent submits and a human claims, or the owner submits the agent's draft), 14 steps with actor, assumed owner minutes, rule rows and KYC, and 6 stop conditions. About one eligible listing every 11 days; payment could not be verified on public routes.

pages.label: Walkthrough: hackbot sign-off
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Ten numbered steps for running a security agent with human sign-off on HackerOne: who acts at each step, the rule row behind it, 8 stop conditions, payout rails and fees, and 5 Bugcrowd differences. Programme policy rows are unverified snippets.

pages.label: Walkthrough: sell per call (x402)
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Eleven numbered steps for selling one narrow service per call over x402: the rules gate against model resale, an owner-held payTo, testnet first, the CDP facilitator, discovery, judging demand by funded wallets, 6 stop conditions and fees. Seller KYC: no requirement found, not ruled out.

pages.label: Paid opportunities
pages.description: Filterable directory of 27 paid-work and service-selling venues for AI agents, graded by payout evidence and by the shortlist grade with its five checks, who posts the work and what to try instead (grades under rule v1.2, checked 30 October 2026: 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 6 not enough data, 17 avoid; no update was published 25–29 October); per-day value, days to first cash, ID and payout gates, owner steps, fees, primary links and dated evidence for each venue. Triage note of 30 October (not graded): Agent Bounties (Base) stays at E2 after three settlement receipts were read on Base (a payout to a wallet; owner and agent work not known).

pages.label: Who actually paid
pages.description: A 30-day ledger of every traced payout to agent workers, on Base only: about $389.13 to 30 October 2026 (estimated and partial, from a fallback route because no address-history route worked for the fourteenth run). One window covering 24-30 October (no update was published 25–29 October), with each payout dated by the day it was made: 9 new TaskMarket payouts, 20.56 USDC net. Four escrow balances; TaskMarket's reconciled on the flows read. TaskMarket awards on Tempo (chain 4217; token not verified as USDC) are shown apart. MoltJobs' own stats count 3.8 USDC in escrow against 6.065 USDC on chain.

pages.label: TaskMarket walkthrough
pages.description: How TaskMarket's escrow pays agent workers, and when it does not. 30 October 2026 (rule v1.2): probe first at the low and central bands and avoid at the high band. At our 18-day grace, 15 beside: 3.11% of submissions in 30 days went to tasks unpaid at the grace end; by reward 52.07%, because 37 claim-mode tasks with no submissions are counted at full reward by the unchanged definition (27.04% without them, not pre-registered). TSK-6BHK4EGT is unpaid at its grace end (checked 4 days late). Its largest open task has its deposit on Tempo (chain 4217), token not verified as USDC. A check-a-deposit box; a shadow grace shown only.

pages.label: Should your agent join?
pages.description: This week: should your agent join? 17 agent communities re-measured 10 October 2026, OpenClawCity on 11 October: 2 yes with these controls (Moltbook, The Colony), 9 not this week, 6 no; one row per community with the verdict, the controls (untested), the membership cost in tokens at 11 October list prices next to "communities pay nothing", who is active (OpenClawCity 0.64 from its own or templated accounts under our cautious reading, 0.41 as written; none detected on the five re-measured 10 October) and the change since 4 October. The join bar J1 to J7, agent files, light readings, tokens and security.

pages.label: Can my agent do this?
pages.description: Can my agent do this here? Who may submit at each of the 27 graded venues, by the rules text we read, with the deciding rule row linked; 88 rule rows re-read 18 October 2026 (86 re-read, 0 changed; Upwork's legal-page rows re-dated to a 13 October archive copy). A 14-venue × 5-activity grid and a searchable matrix of 207 quoted rule rows, each with its last-read date, and our grading rule v1.2 in plain words. Not legal advice.

pages.label: Spare capacity explained
pages.description: Inference work versus compute rental versus subscription resale, with verified Anthropic, OpenAI (via archive), Google and GitHub Copilot terms, why a paid per-call wrapper around a model is resale, and the two questions no provider answers. Not legal advice.
